clue.text: Having some saving graces?

parts.note: a 'saving grace' is usually a redeeming virtue, but here the virtue is literally being good at saving money

explanation.surface: A wry remark about someone who has a few redeeming qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'saving grace' means a redeeming feature; read literally, a grace for saving is economy with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careful and economical with money has the virtue of saving, which is frugality.

clue.text: Nectar may produce a state of ecstasy

indicators.note: the letters of the clue's first word may be worked up into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The drink of the gods might send you into rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may produce' is the anagram signal on NECTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapt, dreamlike condition of rapture or absorption is a classic meaning of the word.

clue.text: Engineers class again make an impression in print

definitions.text: again make an impression in print

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a type is a class or kind

explanation.surface: Engineering students in a class print something again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' looks as if it belongs with 'class', but it opens the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To key text in once more is to produce its printed impression a second time.

clue.text: Special coach for top students?

definitions.meaning: a premium railway carriage, punning on the top grade of British university degree

explanation.surface: A tutor who handles only the brightest pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a tutor, but it is a railway carriage; the top honours degree in Britain is called a first.
explanation.definitionFit: The premium travel category and the highest degree classification both carry this excellent-quality label.

clue.text: Off-peak call?

parts.note: an 'off-peak call' sounds like a cheap phone call, but here it is a cry sung off a mountain peak

explanation.surface: A cheap-rate telephone call made in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-peak is telephone-tariff language; read literally it is a shout from a mountaintop in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The warbling Alpine song of herdsmen echoes from the mountains, a call from a peak.

clue.text: Road surface that makes crawler come to complete stop

parts.note: an asp is a snake, a creature that crawls
to halt is to come to a complete stop

explanation.surface: Tarmac so sticky that a slow vehicle grinds to a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a slow vehicle, but it is the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitumen-based blacktop is the standard material for paving highways.

clue.text: Lancaster ruins inherited from forebears

indicators.note: to ruin the word Lancaster is to wreck its order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A family seat at Lancaster, now in ruins, passed down the generations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed down from ancestors belongs to the family line by heritage.

clue.text: Display that had a dour following in French society

definitions.text: that had a dour following in French society
definitions.meaning: put 'a dour' after this word and you get Madame de Pompadour, a famous figure of the French court

explanation.surface: A show put on by a gloomy hanger-on in Parisian high society.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame de Pompadour was mistress of Louis XV; the second half asks for the word that 'a dour' followed in her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial splendour and show is a grand public display.

clue.text: Display wines duty-free here?

parts.note: to air something is to display it
port is a fortified wine, so wines are ports

explanation.surface: A shop showing off bottles of wine at a tax-free counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty-free here?' defines by example: tax-free shops are found where you fly from.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax-free shopping is a fixture of terminals where passengers board flights abroad.

clue.text: Local vessels, normally handled singly

parts.note: 'local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, and these drinking mugs each have just one handle

explanation.surface: Boats in the harbour that are usually crewed by one sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests boats, but they are pots; in Britain 'the local' is your nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Large one-handled beer mugs are the drinking vessels of the traditional pub.

clue.text: Play-boy?

parts.note: a playboy is a rich pleasure-seeker, but split it reads as a male who is in a play

explanation.surface: A wealthy man who lives for pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Splitting 'playboy' at the hyphen gives a boy of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A male performer on stage is literally a man of the play.

clue.text: Collected tales, edited, about English PM

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short form for edited is read backwards

parts.note: David Cameron was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: An anthology of stories put together around a prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the short form of edited round. The answer is Boccaccio's book of a hundred stories, not an edited collection in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century work is an anthology of a hundred stories told by ten people.

clue.text: IST tycoon

parts.note: the three letters are printed in upper case, so they are capital letters spelling I, S, T

explanation.surface: A bare acronym beside a business magnate, like a headline caption.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a picture: IST written in capitals reads as capital IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy business magnate is a classic owner of capital and investor in enterprise.

clue.text: New star former county's backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the county's name is read backwards

parts.note: Avon was an English county from 1974 to 1996, around Bristol

explanation.surface: A rising celebrity backed by a county that no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: AVON was an English county around Bristol, abolished in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: A star that suddenly flares to great brightness takes the Latin word for new as its name.

clue.text: Opportunity to put one in the picture?

definitions.text: Opportunity to put one in the picture?

parts.words: Opportunity to put one in the picture?
parts.note: 'put in the picture' means inform, but literally it means casting someone in a film

explanation.surface: A chance to bring someone up to date on events.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'put in the picture' means to brief someone; the literal reading is a film role.
explanation.definitionFit: An audition on camera decides whether an actor will be cast in a film.

clue.text: Those chosen courted coming unstuck, getting killed

parts.note: the elect are those chosen

indicators.note: coming unstuck means falling apart, so the letters of courted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doomed romance: the chosen ones' wooing falls apart and ends fatally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming unstuck' reworks COURTED into ROCUTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Death by electric shock is one specific way of being put to death.

clue.text: Sweet thing that's often in a bar and sometimes drunk

definitions.text: Sweet thing that's often in a bar and sometimes drunk

parts.words: Sweet thing that's often in a bar and sometimes drunk
parts.note: a 'sweet thing' drinking in a bar sounds like a person, but this confection comes in bars and as a hot drink

explanation.surface: A charming person who frequents pubs and sometimes gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet thing', 'bar' and 'drunk' all suggest a person at a pub; the confection is sold in bars and made into a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa-based confectionery is sold as bars and also served as a hot beverage.

clue.text: The brave country?

parts.note: '... the Brave' is a famous patriotic song, often played on bagpipes

explanation.surface: A nation known for its courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The well-known song 'Scotland the Brave' is an unofficial Scottish anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation north of England is hailed as brave in the title of its popular anthem.

clue.text: They'd give seasoned advice seeing lads lost at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters of lads lost are jumbled

explanation.surface: Boys lost on the ocean receive guidance from experienced hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasoned' hints at long experience at sea; 'at sea' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Veteran sailors, being experienced, are the people to offer wise counsel.

clue.text: Show indifference to the lamb on Monday?

definitions.meaning: to snub or ignore someone deliberately
a joint of lamb roasted for Sunday lunch is eaten cold the next day

explanation.surface: Ignoring the leftover meat at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Sunday roast leftovers are traditionally eaten cold on Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is a familiar idiom; literally, a joint of lamb served chilled from yesterday.

clue.text: Sorcery makes five ducks go to five hundred ducks

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, so two ducks are OO
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
again two noughts, two O's

explanation.surface: A spell that turns a handful of birds into a huge flock.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, so ducks become O letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic associated with Caribbean religious practice is a form of witchcraft.

clue.text: Wit shown by animated priest

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so the letters of priest are stirred about

explanation.surface: A lively clergyman shows a sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word for liveliness of mind is used for quick cleverness.

clue.text: Cricket trial?

definitions.meaning: an international cricket match lasting up to five days

explanation.walkthrough: An international five-day cricket match is called a Test.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-day international cricket match shares its name with an exam or trial.

clue.text: Outstanding arc-lights?

parts.note: a bow is an arc, a curved shape
lights are windows, the panes that let light in

explanation.surface: Brilliant electric lamps used on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: Arc-lights are powerful lamps; split, 'arc' is a curve and 'lights' are windows, and 'outstanding' means sticking out from the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved bays of glass projecting from a house front literally stand out from the wall.

clue.text: Flourish as one in union

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for a join

parts.note: a weld is a union of two pieces of metal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Thriving as a member of a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' looks like 'thrive' but means brandish.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish or wave a sword about is to handle it with a flourish.

clue.text: A parson must be upset to swear

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the clergyman's title is read backwards

parts.note: REV is the abbreviation for Reverend, the title of a parson

explanation.surface: An upset vicar is driven to use bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be upset' turns the clergyman's title round; 'swear' here means affirm solemnly, not curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly or affirm something as true is to swear to it.

clue.text: Moderate priest pursuing a line at end of service

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the priest follows the opening letters

parts.note: Levi was a priest of the tribe of Levites in the Bible

indicators.note: the end of the word service is its final letter

explanation.surface: A mild clergyman follows the order of service to its close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' is a verb here, meaning ease; LEVI is the Biblical priestly tribe's founder.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease or lessen pain is to moderate it.

clue.text: Duck down after it gives cover

definitions.meaning: a large sea duck of northern coasts
put 'down' after this word and you get a quilted bed covering

explanation.surface: Duck down when something offers you shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: An eiderdown is a quilt; the second half asks for the word that 'down' completes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea duck whose soft breast feathers fill quilts is the bird in question.

clue.text: Merit of French translation of verse

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: a translation renders the word in a new form, so the letters of verse are rearranged

explanation.surface: The worth of a French version of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' reworks VERSE into SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be worthy of a reward is to earn or merit it.

clue.text: Tried to set about making huge car port

indicators.note: to set something about is to rearrange it, so the letters of tried and to are reordered

explanation.surface: An attempt to build an enormous garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car port' looks like a garage; it is a city, the home of the American car industry, on a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michigan city on the Detroit River is the centre of the American motor industry.
